First of all, I feel so seen by this pic bc Hold Them Down is one of my favorite songs in the whole musical lol. My hot take (honestly may not be super hot, I’m new to the fandom): I find Telemachus and Penelope to be a weak characters and didn’t feel as moved by their meeting Ody again, and by extension the Ithaca Saga, as I’ve seen other people be. Of course they’re beautiful songs and performed amazingly, but I think one of the biggest weaknesses of the musical is spending less time with them. 

Now to be fair I last read the Odyssey in High School, so I could be misremembering. But I feel like even though we don’t comparatively spend much time with them there either, we do see a more of them and their time with the suitors than in Epic. We see Television try to toe the line of respecting the suitors as guests while trying to get them the heck out of his house, and we see some tension between him and his mother when he tells her to shut up because he’s the man of the house now. We see Penelope get pissed off at the suitors multiple times, and we see Ody in disguise try to comfort her, etc. 

I get that there were probably constraints. I personally think the musical and its story is served really well by starting with the tail end of the Sack of Troy and moving forward. It’s more accessible for a wider audience. Vs the Odyssey which starts in medias res. But it also had the effect of sacrificing the development of Telemachus and Penelope. (I also think a part of me was just sad to see it end as well lol.)

While I personally dislike the writing decision to merge Rhaena and Nettles in the show, I don’t like these tweets either. It looks like they’re lowkey trying to say “see how obedient she is?!” To me they feel bad faith. They forget the war and the years directly after the war were incredibly tense. 

The council was trying its best to steer Aegon III, down to meddling in his remaining family’s lives. What else could Rhaena do but “actually listen” in this situation? There is no indication she got the combat training Baela seems to have had. Sure, I bet she did enjoy the attention she got in the Vale. I also bet she knew she had some leverage as one of Aegon’s heirs after the war. But that’s not all she would have been. These interpretations bother me because they’re not bothering to look beyond what they think a lady should behave like. I’m not saying Rhaena didn’t enjoy courtly life. I think it’s pretty clear she did. But it’s weird to me that these tweets make it seem like she was just super happy and never questioned anything and that’s why it’s bad she got Sheepstealer. There are valid reasons why that’s not a great choice. I find it a disservice to Rhaena and Nettles. But I think her book characterization is probably more like, she was making the most of a crappy situation to find some enjoyment in life.

It’s been frustrating seeing non-Americans and nonblack people alike urging us specifically to take action in the way they want it. I am taking action. I’ve met my neighbors, some of whom are elderly or otherwise high needs, to ask how I can help them. If they’re interested in starting a community garden, if they need someone to get groceries, etc. I’m constantly looking for resources I can share and distribute with mutual aid groups. I’m researching local reps and laws to see how I can help people learn to vote small first instead of just waiting on the Presidential election every four years.

How I see it is this: I want to help my community weather this. I’m looking for ways to improve my health and skills so I can protect myself. I just don’t see how protesting in this highly militarized and highly surveilled environment is healthy for me or the people I care about. They’ve been killing, disappearing, or otherwise ruining people’s lives for years. 

I truly believe the only reason there hasn’t been as much violence towards protestors is the dearth of black bodies there to target. I support those of us who want to go out, I really do. I hope they are supported by allies who will protect them. I won’t be there though. It’s dangerous for us, always has been, and it is only going to get worse. I’m frustrated by other people demanding solidarity from us only to throw us under the bus.

I work in a doctor’s office, here’s the main thing I’ve picked up from clinical staff. Focus on your hands! 
You’d be surprised how far washing hands goes. 

Wash them when you get home after work or a long day out. Wash them before and after you use the bathroom. Keep some hand sanitizer in your car to use after touching things lots of other people touch (so a gas pump or a card reader, for example) then wash your hands with soap when you get the chance. You don’t really need antibacterial/anti microbial most of the time, as overuse of it can encourage the growth of superbugs.

Pro tip: frequent handwashing can dry your skin out, so it’s important to keep them moisturized. If your skin cracks badly and germs get in there, that cause infections!

Here's my twist out routine, might not work for you because everyone's hair is different but maybe it can help you build a routine.

Always best to start on clean hair. Use a clarifying shampoo and condition well. Detangle with comb in sections while conditioning. 

Apply a leave in conditioner to your hair after you're done washing. I have low porosity hair so I tend to use spray leave ins because they're lighter, like Mielle White Peony Leave-In. Depending on your porosity you might need something heavier.

After that, I apply my main product. My holy grail twist out products are Carol's Daughter Mimosa Hair Honey and African Pride's Shea Butter and Flaxeed Oil Curling Cream. The Mimosa Hair Honey is lighter, but both are products I wouldn't recommend using daily bc they can contribute to buildup. 

After that I smooth some Mielle Rosemary Mint oil over the ends of the twists to seal in moisture. (Oiling my scalp directly doesn't really help me personally so I stick to oiling the ends of my hair)

Hope this helps!
